plan.topic: Dropped your tirzepatide single-dose pen, or it looks damaged: what the Instructions for Use say, and what to do if you're unsure
plan.angle: Sentence 1: 'Dropped your tirzepatide pen? Here's what the pen guide says.' Quote or paraphrase only the IFU's damage wording that you confirm in the loaded Zepbound and Mounjaro single-dose pen IFUs, each with its own URL and revised date. If neither IFU loads, give no sourced IFU claim. Use only the untagged line 'Not sure it's OK? Don't use it. Ask your pharmacist or call the number in your leaflet.' Don't cite the PI storage section for damage. Keep the scope card 'US single-dose pen; KwikPens and vials have their own leaflets.' Close: 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', then the loop line.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide Pen Dropped on the Floor: Still OK? #shorts
plan.why: Visible pen moment for the 08:00 slot, matching the winning pen Shorts (pen blood 170, 888 on TikTok). A new moment not covered in the last 30 days. | fact-check: It's useful and safe as long as it doesn't over-claim. Two risks. (1) I'm not confident the US single-dose pen IFU talks about 'dropped' pens at all. Its usual wording is about not using a pen that looks damaged, frozen, or has cloudy or particle-containing medicine. Never put 'dropped' in the IFU's mouth unless the loaded IFU actually says it. (2) The planned fallback won't work. The PI's How Supplied/Storage section (Zepbound PI, 28 Aug 2026) covers storage and temperature, not damage. Citing it for a 'damaged pen' paraphrase would tag a line to a source that doesn't say it. The search keyword 'tirzepatide pen' covers both brands, so cite Mounjaro's single-dose pen IFU too. No sourcing of replacement pens and no dose or missed-dose talk.

factcheck.summary:
The script passes. It makes one sourced claim, and that claim checks out: Section 2 of both the Zepbound and Mounjaro US prescribing information says to inspect the medicine visually before use. It should look clear and colorless to slightly yellow, and you shouldn't use it if you see particles or discoloration. Both Lilly PDF links loaded, but their text couldn't be extracted. I confirmed the sentence through search results that quote the Zepbound label and index the FDA label PDFs. The Mounjaro wording matches. The revision dates (28 Aug 2026 and 27 Aug 2026) match our known dates; I couldn't read them from the PDFs.

The rest is safe. The writer correctly makes no claim about what the pen leaflet says about dropped pens. The cracked-or-broken line, the "not sure? don't use it" rule and the pharmacist line are our own careful tips with no source tag, which is correct. Nothing in it covers dosing, swapping or stopping medicine. The scope card names the single-dose pen and separates KwikPens and vials. The script has the required "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber." card, no subscribe or link line, no digits in the narration, and about 117 words.

There's one minor framing fix in s1. The label's check is a routine before every dose, not advice written for dropped pens, so the hook shouldn't suggest the label talks about drops.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits right at the top of the target window under speech (-13.5 dB), so a modest +1.15x lift mainly helps the quiet pauses (-17.8 dB) without pushing speech-bed level out of range. Thinned duplicate stock cues (same sound twice at one timestamp) across nearly every transition to stay under the 3–4-effects-per-second rule, pulled down three cues that were too loud during speech (i14 swoosh/tick at -7.9 dB, i47 pop at -7.5 dB), and nudged up an under-level pause tick (i46) that had fallen to -30.5 dB; a few "swell" cues (i13/i27/i40) are essentially inaudible (-50 to -60 dB) and can't be rescued with gain alone, so they were left for the mix engine to re-render rather than masked. Added three neutral custom accents (pen clatter, reassurance chime, page turn) for the dropped-pen and guide-reference beats — no injection, needle, syringe or pill sounds, per the medical-safety rule.
